"### Chart Analysis: Net International Reserves

The chart tracks **Net International Reserves** in billions of US dollars from January 2023 to June 2024. It compares the **Target (7th review)** against the **Actual** performance.

#### Chart Metadata
*   **Title:** Net International Reserves
*   **Subtitle:** Billions of US$, at program rates; cumulative 2/
*   **Y-Axis:** Billions of US$, ranging from -15 to 15 in increments of 5.
*   **X-Axis:** Monthly intervals from Jan-23 to Jun-24.

#### Target vs. Actual Data Points (Approximated from Chart)

| Period | Target (7th review) [Billions US$] | Actual Performance Trend [Billions US$] |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Jan-23 – Mar-23** | ~2.0 | Started at ~5.0, dropped to ~0 by March. |
| **Apr-23 – Jun-23** | ~7.0 | Fluctuated around 0 to -2.0; failed to meet target. |
| **Jul-23 – Sep-23** | ~-2.0 | Continued decline from ~-5.0 to ~-7.0. |
| **Oct-23 – Dec-23** | ~1.5 | Sharp decline, reaching a low of ~-14.5 in December. |
| **Jan-24 – Mar-24** | ~6.0 | Significant recovery, rising from ~-12.0 to ~7.0. |
| **Apr-24 – Jun-24** | ~9.0 | Continued upward trend, peaking at ~12.0 before settling near 10.0. |

#### Summary of Trends
*   **2023 Performance:** Actual reserves consistently underperformed against the targets set in the 7th review. Reserves entered negative territory in March 2023 and suffered a precipitous drop in the final quarter of the year, hitting a bottom of approximately -$14.5 billion in December 2023.
*   **2024 Recovery:** There was a sharp reversal starting in January 2024. Actual reserves crossed back into positive territory in early 2024 and surpassed the program targets by April 2024, reaching a peak of approximately $12 billion."
